definitions: A unit of measurement used in computed tomography (CT) scans to express the radiodensity of a tissue. It is named after Sir Godfrey Hounsfield, one of the developers of the CT scanner.
Sir Godfrey Newbold Hounsfield (1919–2004), a British electrical engineer who shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his role in developing the CT scanner.
examples: Hounsfield developed the first clinical CT scanner.
The Hounsfield scale ranges from -1000 (air) to +1000 (dense bone).
